evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want to register and log in from app startup so that I can access personalized features.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.78. The story has clear user value and mostly objective Gherkin-style criteria. Independence is good but downstream value depends on personalized features existing. It combines registration and login, which are distinct authentication capabilities and may include several edge cases, reducing Small and Estimable scores. Acceptance criteria are testable at a high level but omit field rules, session behavior, duplicate accounts, validation, and recovery flows.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want to select my favorite clubs and preferred sports channels so that I receive content relevant to my interests.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.84. The value proposition is strong and the criteria cover save and update behavior. It has a partial dependency on authentication/profile personalization and later content personalization features. Scope is reasonably small, though it covers both clubs and channels. Estimation is feasible, but details such as valid preference lists, maximum selections, persistence rules, and cross-device behavior are unspecified.

evaluations.user_story: As a football fan, I want to view current news for my favorite teams and selected channels so that I can stay informed from one central app.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.77. The story delivers clear user value and is focused on one news-viewing capability. It partially depends on preference selection and news-feed availability. Estimability and testability are reduced because terms such as "current," "relevant," and "selected channels" need objective ranking, freshness, source, and fallback rules. Acceptance criteria cover preference and no-preference paths but lack deterministic expected content rules.

evaluations.user_story: As a live match follower, I want to see live results and match events for my favorite teams so that I can track matches in real time.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.82. The story is valuable and mostly focused on live ticker consumption. It depends on an external API and selected teams/matches but can be delivered as a coherent capability. Estimation is possible, though update frequency, event types, latency expectations, API contract, and error states are not fully specified. Testability is acceptable but "real time" and "continues to update" need measurable timing thresholds.

evaluations.user_story: As a football information seeker, I want to browse leagues, competitions, teams, and players so that I can access detailed football information at any time.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.70. The story has clear value and is largely independent. However, it is broad, spanning leagues, competitions, teams, and players, which is closer to an epic or feature set than a small story. Estimability is reduced because data fields, navigation depth, search/filter expectations, and supported entities are unspecified. Acceptance criteria are testable only at a superficial level because "requested information" and "available player details" are not objectively defined.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want to access live stream links when broadcasts begin and rights allow it so that I can quickly find where to watch live football.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.82. The story provides clear user value and is focused on displaying eligible stream links. It has dependencies on match/broadcast metadata, rights rules, country detection, and link sources. Estimation is moderately constrained by missing details around rights validation, geolocation, link expiry, and broadcast start timing. Acceptance criteria are generally objective, but the eligibility conditions require precise business rules to be fully deterministic.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want to enable notifications for my favorite teams so that I receive timely updates about news and results.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.73. The story has clear value and leaves implementation choices open. Independence is limited because it relies on favorite-team selection, notification permissions, event generation, and push infrastructure. Estimability is reduced by unspecified event types, timing expectations, platform permissions, opt-out behavior, and delivery failure handling. Testability is partial because "timely" and "relevant" need measurable definitions.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want to share news and game reports through social media so that I can distribute interesting football content to others.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.85. The story is focused, relatively small, and has clear user value. It partially depends on shareable news/report content and device-level sharing capabilities. The story is somewhat prescriptive by naming social media, but still leaves implementation reasonably negotiable. Acceptance criteria are objective, though supported sharing channels, content payload format, and failure handling could be defined more explicitly.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want the app’s modules to be accessible through one interface so that I can quickly reach the information I need.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.57. The story expresses meaningful navigation value, but it is highly dependent on the existence and readiness of multiple app modules. It is broad and integration-oriented, making it closer to a UI/navigation epic than a small independent story. Estimability and testability are weakened by vague terms such as "one interface," "integrated," and "accessible manner" without measurable accessibility or navigation criteria. The live ticker scenario is more concrete but depends on another module.

evaluations.user_story: As a user, I want the app to remain usable when my connection drops so that I can continue accessing available functionality.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.58. The user value is clear and the implementation remains negotiable. However, the story is broad because offline behavior can affect authentication, navigation, cached content, live data, preferences, and error handling across the app. Independence is limited by dependencies on many modules. Estimability and testability are reduced because "usable" and "functionality that does not require an active server response" are not enumerated. The live-data offline scenario is objective, but the general offline scenario needs specific supported functions and expected states.

evaluations.user_story: As a product stakeholder, I want user feedback and app reviews to be evaluated continuously so that functionality can be improved over time.
evaluations.reasoning: Overall INVEST mean: 0.62. The story has stakeholder/business value but mixes a system capability with an operational process, reducing clarity. "Evaluated continuously" and "perform an evaluation activity" are vague and make estimation difficult. The scope may include ingestion, aggregation, reporting, workflow, and manual review processes, so it is not clearly small. Acceptance criteria are partially testable for presence or absence of feedback inputs, but relevant channels, evaluation cadence, outputs, and system-versus-process responsibilities need definition.
